detail.longDescription: I am competing in a competition named "Do not Overfit! II" . This competition has a train dataset of 250 rows and approximately 300 columns, a test dataset of 19,750 rows and approximately 300 columns and a submission dataset which has 19750 rows and 2 columns namely ID and target . Let me tell you that the target is binary classification and all the other columns are numerical values. Also, there is a class imbalance problem because the target has 66.66% of 0s and 33.33% of 1s. Also, remember that the issues faced are that there are no column names, so we cannot use any domain-specific description so we cannot use domain specific knowledge to select the features. Now my questions are: Do I need to use SMOTE, or is there any other method to reduce the class imbalance or Is this class imbalance not a big deal given that the training dataset is much less? Does this size of the dataset effect on selecting whether to treat class imbalance or not? If there is another dataset with the same class imbalance but the datset is too huge would you still like to treat class imbalance or will you build the model leaving it as it is Does SMOTE works on categorical datasets when the number of columns present are more with limited available rows? How do I select the best features out of these columns when we do not know anything about them? How do I know to select only these many number of features? Why should I select only those features? How can I determine that this is the best output for my question?(Which features to select and how many to select) I am using K-Fold Stratified train-test splits for this so that the model could be trained better(I am using this because the data available is quite less compared to the testing data). Is my choice correct, or are there any better choices that would be even more useful? I would appreciate any suggestions or explanations regarding the above questions
